title: How Does RL Post-training Induce Skill Composition? A Case Study on Countdown
abstract: arXiv:2512.01775v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: While reinforcement learning (RL) successfully enhances reasoning in large language models, its role in fostering compositional generalization (the ability to synthesize novel skills from known components) is often conflated with mere length generalization. To this end, we study what RL post-training teaches about skill composition and how the composition structure affects the skill transfer. We focus on the Countdown task (given n numbers and a target, form an expression that evaluates to the target) and analyze model solutions as expression trees, where each subtree corresponds to a reusable subtask and thus can be viewed as a "skill." Tracking tree shapes and their success rates over training, we find: (i) out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization to larger n and to unseen tree shapes, indicating compositional reuse of subtasks; (ii) the order of skill acquisition depends upon the composition structure---models master shallow balan

translated_title: 强化学习后训练如何诱导技能组合？——以Countdown任务为例的案例研究
translated_abstract: 虽然强化学习（RL）成功提升了大型语言模型的推理能力，但其在促进组合泛化（即从已知组件合成新技能的能力）方面的作用，常与单纯的长度泛化相混淆。为此，我们研究了RL后训练在技能组合方面究竟教会了模型什么，以及组合结构如何影响技能迁移。我们聚焦于Countdown任务（给定n个数字和一个目标值，构造一个运算结果等于目标值的表达式），并将模型解答解析为表达式树，其中每个子树对应一个可复用的子任务，因而可被视为一种“技能”。通过跟踪树形状及其成功率随训练的变化，我们发现：(i) 模型能对更大的n以及未见过的树形状实现分布外（OOD）泛化，表明子任务被组合式复用；(ii) 技能习得的顺序取决于组合结构——模型先掌握浅层平衡（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 本文通过将Countdown任务中模型的解答解析为表达式树，发现RL后训练能诱导模型对子任务技能进行组合式复用（实现对更大规模和未见结构的分布外泛化），且技能习得的顺序由任务的组合结构决定。
en_tdlr: By analyzing model solutions as expression trees on the Countdown task, this paper shows that RL post-training induces compositional reuse of subtask skills—enabling OOD generalization to larger inputs and unseen structures—and that the order of skill acquisition is determined by the task's composition structure.
